Understanding Your Role

Understanding Your Role

Welcome to the Georgia Urology Patient Support Center! Your role as a Patient Support Center Representative is a multi-leveled problem-solving position. Once you are released to the “floor” to start taking calls on your own, you will be expected to create positive and patient focused experiences. You are the first point-of-contact for our patients, which means what you do has a huge impact! Think of yourself as a patient liaison, connecting callers to needed services and providing guidance through the appointment making process. Patient Support Center Representatives are Expected to: Demonstrate Positive Customer Service • Use Resources Critically and Creatively • Effectively Communicate with Patients and Staff • Take Ownership This Scheduling Foundations Guide is a resource for information on the Patient Support Center’s procedures.

02

Customer Service

Active Listening

One of the most important skills you can have in the medical scheduling setting is listening. From accurately creating patient’s chart to messaging clinical staff about life changing medication, everything falls back to being an active and resourceful listener for your caller. Active listening promotes positive engagement and ensures that you fully tune in to your caller’s wants and can anticipate their needs. This is a skill that requires intentional practice in your customer service routine. Active listening is the conscious practice of non-judgmental listening with goal of clarity and understanding. The Key Traits of Active Listening

  • Listening patiently-keep communication open by avoiding. interruptions while someone else is speaking o Listen for various tones and emotions that can give more insight about the caller’s requests o Listen and make note of key information to address of the caller’s needs • Listening with a clear mind- avoid thinking of responses while the other person is speaking, just listen and absorb what the speaker has to say
  • Offer solutions that are related to. caller’s request
  • Summarizing- repeating back what speaker has. told you ensures that you understand the speak and gives the speaker confidence that they are being heard
  • Using confirmation phrases o Example 1. Yes, please continue o Example 2: I understand your point of view
  • Maintain non-judgement- remember your goal is. to reach mutual understanding! In order to do that respect must be practiced.

Confidence and Foresight

Having confidence is an especially important trait develop as you problem solve our callers’ requests. Knowledge or confidence in your services and product make an immense difference in trust that your customers have in your company. Being prepared to answer questions before they are even asked can really enhance that level of trust.

  • Example A. A patient states that they live in a city that you have never heard of before. As soon as you hear that city’s name, look it up on Google maps and determine which offices are closest and most convenient. Doing so creates better a chance the patient will be impressed you already know which location would be ideal.
  • Example B. A patient would like to be seen at a specific office that is rarely visited by the desired provider. There will not be an opening for quite some time. After finding the first availability at that location, also find a sooner availability at another nearby office. Having this additional option ready will indirectly inform the caller that you have gone the extra mile by having a “Plan B” at their disposal. Some ways you increase your confidence in this role are
  • Familiarizing yourself with trends in the. physicians’ schedule
  • Having a clear grasp on using. the Preference Guideline and Insurance Grid • Identifying additional resources that will support you while scheduling (Floor support, the Georgia Urology website, emails announcing updated information, etc.)
  • Organizing notes and creating a record. of answers to questions you come across As your confidence grows in this position your foresight, the ability to plan and anticipate customer needs, will grow also!

Self- Awareness

Self-awareness is your ability to identify your actions and motivations. This skill especially crucial as you navigate solving patient inquiries and issues. Throughout of your shift you are expected to treat every call like it is your first call of the day. This means maintaining a consistent level of welcoming enthusiasm and openness with your callers. Having an increased self-awareness can support your ability to perform successfully and create positive experiences during the day. You can break self-awareness down into three levels:

  • Thinking- identifying thoughts and emotions in. order to understand and adjust mental reactions o Can be achieved with meditation, self-questioning, and emotion labeling for example
  • Voicing- organizing your thoughts. beliefs, and attitudes with a visual medium o Can be achieved with writing, completing personality tests, and vision boards for example
  • Implementing- analyzing past actions and deciding. how to handle future situations o Can be achieved with honest self-reflections, feedback from trusted people, and performance evaluations for example Check in with yourself throughout the day! You can self-assess your current thoughts/emotions, beliefs/attitudes, and behaviors/decisions. Taking inventory of your mental state can help you prevent errors, avoid burnout, master your resources, and remain solution oriented.

Relationship Development

Establishing a relationship in a customer service roll is both a crucial and vital for success across the board, particularly in the medical field! With patients and your coworkers alike, you want to create a positive experience for those you interact with. It significantly impacts how responsive and receptive others are, especially in special circumstances. When it comes to relationship development overall, you want to express to the respective party in every way possible that you are someone they can trust, and that you have their needs and wants taken into full consideration with confidence! Starting Relationships in a Positive Place Find common ground by showing care o Ask your coworkers/callers about their interests o Acknowledge significant events (achievements, birthdays, holidays, etc.) o Check in on your coworker’s/caller’s well being Be accountable and reliable o Promptly respond to messages sent to you o Show up to work consistently and on time o Be proactive about your responsibilities Show gratitude o Express appreciation to those that assist you o Give credit to others for their contributive efforts o Openly value constructive feedback and suggestion Practice transparent and respectful communication o Confront issues in a professional manner o Converse with the goal of understanding o Do not make up answers to inquiries, ask for assistance or seek more information

03

Greetings and Wrap Ups

Incoming Calls

There are three main components to the standard incoming call greeting, each serving a specific purpose. Remember you are the first point of contact for the caller and this may be their first experience with Georgia Urology. We must intentionally communicate our focus on patient care from the start. On an incoming call your introduction would include three primary components. • Thank you for calling Georgia Urology. o We must brand the call. This also confirms with the caller that they have reached the right place for assistance. • This is (your name) . o We must identify ourselves on every call, there are no exceptions. Patients appreciate the opportunity to speak with a live person when making an appointment or seeking a solution to an inquiry. Sharing our names create a personable experience for the caller. • Whom do I have the pleasure of speaking with? o Please make note of this information and use caller’s name throughout the call. Having the caller identify themselves serves multiple purposes. Using the caller’s name creates a positive connection during your interaction. Additionally, names serve as the foundation for locating patient information in NextGen or determining whether a caller is new to our practice. Sometimes a caller is scheduling an appointment or requesting information on a patient’s behalf, and we need that caller’s identification to verify HIPPA authorization. Once you confirm the caller’s name and it to the details of any appointment you schedule.

Calls Backs

Callers trying to reach our services have the option to request a “call back” from us. Instead of waiting on hold until they can speak with someone, our system will save their place in the queue line and make an outgoing call to their number. As you are answering calls, you will be able to recognize a call back when you hear an automated voice say the phrase, “Please wait while the call is established.” In these occurrences, we want to verbally acknowledge that our system is making an outgoing call to the patient by adopting to the following greeting: “This is _____(your name)_________ from Georgia Urology returning your call. How can I help you?” Sometimes the caller may not be available at the time of the call. In that case please leave the following message on the caller’s voicemail: "This is Georgia Urology returning your call if you still need assistance please call us back, we are experiencing longer than normal wait times but we ask that you hold for an agent. We appreciate your patience and thank you for choosing Georgia Urology.”

Outbound Calls

There are times when you will need to make an outbound call to get in touch with a patient to reschedule, confirm information, or reconnect with a lost call. In those cases, you will still introduce yourself, state your connection with Georgia Urology, as well as confirm the identity of the answering individual. “Good morning/Good afternoon this is __(your name) with Georgia Urology. Am I speaking with Mr./Ms. ______ ______?” For Pediatric calls: “Good morning/Good afternoon this is (your name) with Georgia Urology. Is this a parent or legal guardian of ________ ________? May I ask your name for my records please?”

Dropped Calls

When we experience technical issues that cause the phone system to drop calls, we need to have a way to alert callers. This is not a full-proof method, but we hope that if the caller is attempting to call us right back, we will have the opportunity to explain the problem that occurred with a consistent and professional response. After we have system crash that causes us to lose a call (that could be actively talking, just starting the call, or the phone was starting to ring on your line). When we answer the next active call, we need to change to the following greeting: “Thank you for calling Georgia Urology. This is (your name) . I am sorry we just experienced a system issue that resulted in us losing calls. I apologize for any inconvenience this may have cause you. How can I help you?” In addition to this greeting, obtain the patient’s name and a contact number in case the technical issue persists, and you must reach back out the patient.

Dead Air

Due to growing use of various call technologies (computer-based phone lines, cell phones, and blue tooth) we sometimes experience “dead air calls.” In order to ensure that we give our patients every opportunity to connect with us we will use the following dead air call protocol:

  • Use the standard phone greeting ---. Wait 30 seconds
  • Do a second abbreviated greeting ---. Georgia Urology this is (your name) . --- Wait another 30 seconds
  • Simply say Hello --- Wait another. 30 seconds We now have given the caller a minute and a half to see if we have connectivity.
  • End the call with the following statement.  Disconnecting call due to no response.

Wrap Ups

Before you end a call after scheduling an appointment you must reconfirm key appointment details. This encourages clear understanding of all that was discussed with the caller. As you are concluding a call you will want to restate following key details:

  • Appointment date time
  • Office location and offer office address
  • Provider being seen
  • Insurance and Identification card requirement
  • Online paperwork will arrive two days. before appointment from Phreesia
  • COVID protocols Your final statements before. you close a call should be: Is there anything else I can help you with? (answer any remaining questions caller may have) Thank you again for calling Georgia Urology. Your wrap up details may change based upon the nature of the call.
  • Confirming a clinic visit Remind patient of appointment date. time, office, and provider Remind patient of Insurance and Identification card requirement Remind patient of Phreesia paperwork procedures Remind patient of COVID protocols
  • Rescheduling a clinic visit Remind patient of appointment date. time, office, and provider Remind patient of Insurance and Identification card requirement Remind patient of Phreesia paperwork procedures Remind patient of COVID protocols
  • Scheduling/Confirming/Rescheduling a Virtual Visit Remind patient. of appointment date, time, office, and provider Confirm patient’s email and cell number is correct Remind patient that they will receive their appointment link 30 minutes prior to their appointment time Remind patient of Phreesia paperwork procedures
04

Call Flow

During the time you pick up your call until the time you hang up the line, you will want to be aware of typical structure of a call’s flow to ensure you are receiving all necessary information from a caller. While every call will not be the same, follow this general guideline to keep organized.

Transferring Calls

Sometimes patients have requests that fall outside the scope of the Patient Support Center. In those cases, you will need to transfer that caller to the appropriate department for further assistance. Note that before you reach out to another department or Floor Support you must create a chart for the patient in NextGen. This will aid the receiving party in best assisting the situation.

  • Warm Transfers Most transfers will be warm transfers. which means that you make contact with a department representative on the caller’s behalf, explain the caller’s needs, and then release the call. To ensure that a patient has the best service experience it is critical for you to make contact with the right department and prepare both the caller and the receiver for a call transfer. o There are some cases in which you may not immediately connect with a department representative. If the department you are trying to reach is currently unavailable, you will hear an explanatory message. Unfortunately, we do not have the capability to wait on hold for extended periods until a representative can get on the line. A. For non-urgent issues (first time calling for request): cold transfer to appropriate department. B. For non-urgent issues (and the caller has previously called about the request): Offer the send an email on the patient’s behalf to the appropriate parties. CC the region’s Practice Administrator, Assistant Practice Administrator, Team Leads, and the Patient Support Center Manager. C. For urgent issues (first time calling): cold transfer to appropriate department D. For urgent issues (and caller has previously called about the request): Attempt to warm transfer. If you receive the busy message, work with Floor Support to transfer/come up with alternative solution Here are some examples of what you can communicate to a caller when you are unable to connect to a department representative. o Triage- for callers needing assistance with symptom assessment, medication requests, or nurse visits The individuals who can assist you with this are our Triage clinicians. I can transfer you to them if you would like. (wait for response) When I complete the transfer, your call will be answered by the first available clinician. There may be a slight wait. You will have the option to leave a message if you are unable to hold. Please stay on the line and I will direct your call to those that can best assist you. Thank you for calling Georgia Urology- I will transfer you now. o Front Office- for callers needing assistance with partial records, rescheduling/cancelling appointments some procedures and nurse visits, office directions and landmarks The individuals who can best assist you with the individuals that are in the office itself. I would like to transfer you to the office if that is ok with you? (wait for response) Thank you for calling Georgia Urology- I will transfer you now. Before transferring always educate your callers about who they are being sent to, what to expect, and ask for permission to complete the process. • Cold Transfers There are few cases in which a cold transfer is most appropriate. This means transferring a call without making an initial effort to connect with a department representative. Note that a cold transfer is not a blind transfer, which means there is no communication with the caller before they are transferred. At Georgia Urology there are no cases in which a blind transfer would be appropriate. Before a transfer is made you must inform the caller why they need to be transferred to a certain department for assistance. The caller must also agree to be transferred. o In most cases, cold transfers are acceptable when a caller needs surgical related assistance, including pre ops, post ops, and surgeries. These calls would be transferred to that POD’s surgery scheduling line. Before transferring inform patient the following: The individuals who can assist you with this are our Surgery Schedulers. I can transfer you to them if you would like. (wait for response) When I complete the transfer, you call will be answered by the first available surgery scheduler. There may be a slight wait. You will have the option to leave a message if you are unable to hold. Please stay on the line and I will direct your call to those that can best assist you. Thank you for calling Georgia Urology- I will transfer you now. o In most cases, cold transfers are also acceptable when a caller needs assistance with payment plans, details of treatment costs, insurance verification or codes, or has an account balance that prevents an appointment being saved on a physician’s schedule. All financial related questions should be transferred to the Central Business Office (ext 1119). Before transferring inform the patient of the following: The individuals who can best assist you are at our Central Business Office. They are equipped to answer questions such as yours. I can connect you to our Central Business Office if you would like. (wait for response) Thank you. There may be a slight wait. Please stay on the line and I will direct your call to those that can best assist you. Thank you for calling Georgia Urology- I will transfer you now. o Cold transfers are also permitted when connecting callers to the Patient Support Spanish queue (1155) and Urolift lines (ext 1108) Every situation is unique, depending upon the nature of the call there may be times when a warm transfer to either of these departments is more appropriate.

Hold Times and Time Management

How long someone holds to have their questions or concerns addressed plays a major role in the trust and respect of whomever you are assisting. If someone is holding for an extensive period they may just hang up and call right back only further complicating the caller's situation. It is important to recognize when someone has been holding for TOO long and additional steps may need to be taken, such as offering to call them back. This way your caller is not having to idly remain tied to their phone. Politely informing a caller that their questions or concerns cannot be answered at this time, and confidently communicating that you will call them back with resolution is sometimes the best course of action. Reaching out to floor support if you are unsure of who you should reach out to can also significantly reduce hold times for callers. A great way to combat long hold times is simply becoming accustomed to your resource materials. The more familiar you are with using your tools and more efficient you will be overall.

Scripts: Expired Patients, Vasectomies, and Circumcisions

  • Expired Patients While we may not. be aware of every caller’s life events, we always want to express empathy and care while scheduling. Some callers may have recently experienced an especially difficult time like a death in the family. When you receive information that one of our patients have passed, it is important to be sensitive and tactful in those moments. It can be hard to know exactly what to say during those times, so use this script as response to that kind of information: I am very sorry for your recent loss and am glad to assist during this difficult period. I can cancel the patient’s/your [specific relation]’s upcoming appointments at this time. May I ask the date of passing for my records? (wait for response) Thank you. (cancel appointments) All upcoming appointments have been cancelled. Is there any other way I can assist you? (wait for response) Thank you for calling Georgia Urology, we express our condolences to you during this time. o Additionally, you will need to mark the patient as expired in the NextGen system. A. If the patient has any upcoming appointments, regardless of appointment type, cancel them, selecting “Deceased” as the cancellation reason B. Add “patient expired per relation” and caller’s name to the appointment details with your initials and date of the entry C. Open the patient from the Lookup function and change their status to “Deceased” D. Check the “Expired” box (on the right of PCP box) and enter date of patient passing
  • Vasectomy Consultations One of the most. common types of appointment you will schedule are vasectomy consultation. Often patients are not aware of Georgia Urology’s process in scheduling this procedure. For patients interested in vasectomies they must first schedule a consultation to discuss the procedure with a physician. Procedure appointments will then be handled with the Ambulatory Surgery Center of that physician's pod. Please state the following when scheduling a vasectomy consultation: I would like to clarify that this appointment is a consultation with the physician. This visit is for you to discuss the details of the vasectomy procedure and receive clarification to any questions you may have. If you decide to move forward with the procedure after your consultation, the physician will then discuss the scheduling process. The procedure can usually be scheduled for 6-8 weeks later.
  • Circumcision Consultations The pediatric side of. the practice receive numerous requests for circumcisions. Like vasectomies, any patient needing a circumcision must have a consultation first before a procedure can be scheduled. It is very important that parents/legal guardians/physician's office understand that when they arrive to that initial appointment, they need to expect a consultation not a procedure. Please state the following when scheduling a circumcision consultation: I would like to clarify that this appointment is a consultation with the physician. This visit is to determine if your child is a surgical candidate for a circumcision. Surgery will not be performed on this day. If your child is determined to be a surgical candidate, the physician will then discuss the process of scheduling the procedure. The procedure can usually be scheduled for 6-8 weeks later.

Looking Up Your Patients

In your call flow, it is crucial that you determine whether a patient is new or established early on in order to best service them in an efficient and organized way. Take the following steps to ensure you have sufficiently distinguished whether a caller is a new or established patient.

Step One: Use Appointment List

Search the patient’s name and date of birth in Appointment List. This can be achieved in multiple ways. NextGen allows some flexibility in how you search for the patient within the system. For example:

  • Enter the full first and/or last name + DOB. click Find
  • Enter first few letters of first and/or last name + DOB. click Find In the example below, the partial first name, full last name, and the DOB was used to find the patient. Patients who have visited one of our providers will have a history of appointments that generate in a list. Once you have located your patient, verify the appointment Date and Status of the most recent appointment.
  • Appointment Date- A patient is considered. established with us as long as their most recent Kept appointment is within three years from time of the current call. In the example above for Paula Test, the patient’s most recent appointment occurred August 21, 2018. This patient will be considered established with us until August 21, 2021 (assuming no other appointments are scheduled before that date). On and after August 22, 2021 this patient will be considered a new patient.
  • Appointment Status- Patients must also keep. their appointment in order to be considered as an established patient. There will be cases in which you will find an appointment history for a patient, but the appointments were no shows or cancellations. If there is no Kept appointment within three years from the time of the call, this patient is considered a new patient. In the example below, this patient made an appointment with us in the past that was ultimately cancelled. If this patient calls back to schedule they would be considered a new patient. Once you have verified that the patient is established with Georgia Urology, proceed to scheduling with the associated provider. If the patient is not found in the system’s records move on to the next step.

Step Two: Use People Lookup

Sometimes when you attempt to search for a patient using the Appointment List tool you may get a result like the example below: A “no records were found” message will appear when there is no appointment history associated with the credentials you have entered. When this happens, you will need to perform further investigative work to verify the patient’s status.

  • It is possible for a caller. to have chart information already in our system, despite not having a listed appointment. o In order to avoid potentially creating duplicate charts in the system, use the People Lookup Tool to verify whether the caller already has a chart in NextGen. Just like the Appointment List Tool, you can search for a patient using a combination of their name and DOB. In the example below, the patient was still not found in the system. In this case, proceed to scheduling a New Patient appointment. o If you search for a patient using the People Lookup Tool and they have a chart in our system. They are still considered a New Patient, because they have yet to be seen by our providers. However, there is no need to create a new chart when scheduling the appointment. Simply lookup the existing chart and update the demographics as necessary.
  • If the caller insists that they. have seen one of our providers before o First, confirm that you have the correct spelling and date of birth. Renter the information in Appointment List, the error could simply be a typo on your part. o Next, inquire if the caller can give you more details like who they have seen in the past, the office they went to, or the date of an appointment. Attempt to search for the patient by using part of their name and/or DOB and another category like Resource, Appointment Date, or Service Location. In the example below, the resource category was used in combination with the caller’s name. o If the above steps yield no results, there could be a typo in NextGen. Ask the caller what number is on their chart and use the People Lookup Tool to search for them in the system. If there is a chart associated with the provided number the patient’s information will open and you may edit any errors that may exist. o Finally, if you are still unable to find the patient in NextGen’s Practice Management side search for the patient in E.H.R.

Identifying New and Established NAUA Patients

In 2020 Georgia Urology merged with North Atlanta Urology Associates (NAUA) as a secondary Lawrenceville location for patients. With this acquisition, Dr. Yeoh and Dr. Goldberg were added to Georgia Urology’s impressive list of providers. This consolidation also included the transfer of NAUA patient charts to Georgia Urology’s current NextGen system. Unfortunately, NAUA patients appointment histories are not always accessible through the Practice Management side of NextGen. There are times when an established NAUA patient will call and there is not appointment history found using Appointment Lookup. The best way to verify a NAUA patient’s status is to look up the patient in E.H.R. and locate the most recent visit from the encounter dates.

Scheduling Procedures

Scheduling Limitations

While there are many ways that we can assist our callers, there are certain services that fall outside of the Patient Support Center’s scope.

  • Patient Support Center Representatives are not. authorized to give medical advice without advance approval. This includes suggesting patients go to an Emergency Room (which Triage and Front Desk are authorized to do). o If a situation calls for medical advice reach out to the clinical staff Triage department.
  • Patient Support Center Representatives are prohibited. from giving Personal Health Information to unauthorized persons.
  • Patient Support Center Representatives cannot place. an incoming on hold prior to gathering the information necessary to service the caller
  • Procedures that we must do. o Patient Support Center Representatives must make a documented effort to call back a lost call o Patient Support Center Representatives must communicate Self-Pay consultation fee and use the Circumcision/Vasectomy scripts

Event Types

There are only a handful of visit types that the Patient Support Center sets up, but there are quite a few other visit types that need to be set up by others.

  • For Nurse visits (labs. bloodwork, tests, in office radiology, BCG, IC treatments, Urodynamics, injections etc.), the triage staff or the front desk staff of that patient's office can schedule these. Transfer these calls to triage or front desk.
  • Procedures such as Vasectomies and Cystoscopies. are typically scheduled by Ambulatory Surgery Center staff (ASC). Front desk can also handle some of these procedures. Transfer these calls to the ASC or front desk.
  • Pre/Post Op/Surgery visits should be scheduled. with the doctor's surgery coordinator. Each doctor typically has one and, in some cases, if they are out of the office, their responsibilities are typically deferred to either another surgery nurse, Triage, or the appropriate practice administrator. Transfer these calls to the Surgery Schedulers. If you receive a request for an appointment that is out of the Patient Support Center’s scope, attempt to contact the appropriate department according to Warm and Cold transfer procedures. DO SCHEDULE DON’T SCHEDULE New Patient Appt (NP) Injections Follow Up Visits (FU) *an appointment for an established patient to follow up with their provider regarding an issue that has already been seen Pre-Ops and Post Ops *a post op is a follow up appointment made within three months of a surgery; if three months have passed since surgery, the appt CAN be scheduled by the PSC as a follow up Transfer Patient Visit (TP) *an appointment for an established patient switching to another provider’s care /// only used for Adult patients Surgeries and Procedures you CAN schedule the consultation Vasectomy Consultation (VasOpinion) Catheter Removals for established patients Consult-Circumcision (CCi) *only used for PEDS patients Lab Draws Stones (Stone11) *stones appointments scheduled within 24-48 hours of the initial call Nurse Visits Interstitial Cystitis Patient (IC) Radiology Confirmed Cancer Consultation (CCa) *event type for established patients only IC Treatments Virtual Visit New/Virtual Visit Follow Up/Virtual Visit Transfer—Virtual Visit (VVN/VVF/VVT) Urine/Semen sample drop offs Note that the same rule applies to appointment changes and cancellations. We cannot reschedule or cancel Nurse Visits, Procedures/Surgeries, or Injections/Tests/Lab work. The caller would need to be transferred to the appropriate department for a cancellation. The exception to this would be if the patient has deceased and we are expiring the patient in NextGen. Special Scheduling Cases None of the Adult providers treat for Hernia. Our Pediatric providers only treat Inguinal Hernia. None of the Pediatric providers treat Erectile Dysfunction (ED). None of our providers treat Protein in Urine if this is the patient’s primary concern.
  1. 3 Creating Charts The first step. to making an appointment is ensuring that we have the patient’s chart in our system. A medical chart is a complete record of a patient’s key clinical data and medical history. The Patient Support Center’s role in chart creation is obtaining basic demographic information.
  • Patient name. DOB, Address, Phone Numbers, Email, Primary Care Physician, Insurance information Typically, charts are created during the appointment making process. To fully create an appointment, you would need some additional information.
  • Referring physician. how the patient heard about us (Marketing), facility patient records are coming from, diagnosis/symptoms Sometimes you may need to create a chart before scheduling an appointment. This can be done through both Practice Management and Electronic Health Records (E.H.R.) systems. See Chapter 15, 15.3 and 15.4 You may need to create a chart before making an appointment when:
  • Reaching out to another department for. assistance- this helps the other party look up the patient’s information and make faster determinations
  • Handling workers compensation requests

Duplicate Charts

On occasion you may discover multiple charts for the same patient. This can be due to name changes, typos while creating the initial chart, address changes, and other variables. When this happens, follow these steps:

  1. Verify that all the information on. these charts are the same or relate to same individual. If you have the patient in question on the phone at the time, ask them to confirm the information with you.
  2. Once you confirmed the duplicate charts are for the same individual. email this information to Mandy Johnson at ajohnson@gaurology.com. Include the patient’s demographic information, so she will be able to easily locate and merge the charts.

Writing Appointment Details

In NextGen each appointment contains a details box allowing for the exchange of information among the Patient Support Center, front desk, clinical staff, and physicians. As the first point of contact, Patient Support Center representatives serve as the primary liaisons of appointment specifics. You may be the last person a patient speaks with before they see their physician, so it is important that key details are gathered from the start.

  • Make sure to include the following in your appointment details. o Appointment Type (NP, TP, CCa, etc.) o Diagnosis/Reason for visit o Scheduling caller (if not the patient) o Recent medical visits related to diagnosis o Records related to diagnosis (can be faxed to office appointment is scheduled in or patient can bring them physically)  If faxed, include contact person and/or number for the facility we are receiving records from  If there are no records include “no records” to details o Special insurance or self-pay circumstances o COVID-19 protocols o Patient paperwork protocols
  • Always end you detail entry with. your initials!
  • Example 1. Diana Burns is scheduling an appointment for a new patient wanting to be seen for frequency. This patient was last seen at Eagles Landing Family Practice. Diana’s appointment details might look like this: NP//frequency//last seen at Eagles Landing Family Practice//Shauna, Eagles Landing front desk will fax records (777-888-9999)//aware to come alone and wear mask//aware to complete paperwork prior DB
  • Example 2. Kenneth Puggs is speaking with a wife (Judy Sanders) wanting to schedule a follow up appointment for her husband for groin pain and testicle tenderness. This patient is an established self-pay patient. Kenneth’s appoint details might look like this: FU//groin pain//testicle tenderness//scheduled with wife (Judy)//self-pay, aware of $250, plus additional fees//aware to come alone and wear mask//aware to complete paperwork prior KP
  • Adding Information to Preexisting Details Sometimes. you will need to update appointment details to reflect changes to the appointment. In those cases, include the current date of your entry, the new information, and end the entry with your initials. o Example: Cheyenne Woode receives a call on August 13, 2020. This patient would like to reschedule his appointment from August 21st to September 9th. Once, Cheyenne moves the patient’s appointment, she would add: “8.13.20 rescheduled per patient CW”

Understanding Insurance

Commercial v. Government Plans

Part of your responsibility when scheduling is confirming that the desired provider accepts the patient’s insurance. Not doing so can result in a patient being turned away from a physician’s office the day of their consultation. Fortunately, this process has a multilevel safeguard with the Patient Support Center acts as the initial manager that is then supported by the Central Business Office. When discussing insurance with a caller it is important to recognize the two insurance types:

  • Commercial (private-funded)- primarily provided through employer-. sponsored plans o HMO, PPO, POS, High-Deductible Health Plan (HDHP), Exclusive Provider Organizations (EPO), Private Fee-For-Service (PFFS)
  • Government (taxpayer funded)- financed by federal. and state taxes o Medicare, Medicaid, Peachstate, Ambetter, Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP), Wellcare, Federal/state employee health plans, Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Tricare Once you have identified the insurance type use the Insurance Grid to confirm the physician’s preference. If a plan is not accepted by the desired provider, patients may either proceed with scheduling as a self-pay patient or schedule with a different provider that does accept their health plan

Insurance Types

If a caller is having a difficult time identifying if their insurance type, direct them to look at the bottom corners of their card. If the caller still struggles default to PPO, the Central Business Office will verify patient insurance information once it is in our system.

  • HMO (Health Maintenance Organization)- Have one. in-network PCP that provides routine care and refers you to in-network specialists. Referrals are required, and out-of-network care will not be covered.
  • EPO (Exclusive Provider Organization)- Similar to HMO. only in-network care is covered. Generally, have larger networks than HMO. Similar to PPO, no referrals required for specialist care.
  • POS (Point of Service)- Have one. in-network PCP that provides routine care and manages your access to other doctors. Referrals to specialists are required. You can also visit other out-of-network physicians at a higher cost.
  • PPO (Preferred Provider Organization)- Not required. to have a PCP and do not need referrals to see specialists. You can choose which doctors you see. Out- ofnetwork physicians will cost more.

Multiplan and Medi-Share

  • Multiplan and PHCS- Nationwide PPO provider. network that allows you to choose which doctors you see. Multiplan and PHCS are not insurance plans, but broad networks of providers. Insurance companies can contract with these networks to access discounted services for their members. o All our Providers accept Multiplan
  • Medi-Share- Healthcare sharing program that consists. of a community sharing financial resources and paying each other’s medical expenses. This is not an insurance plan, but a service a patient may have. o Only our Piedmont Providers and our Pediatric Providers accept MediShare.  Piedmont Providers- Dr. Abbott, Dr. Shapiro, Dr. Yang, Dr. Barett- Harlow, Donica Davis P.A., Dr. Kemper, Dr. Chen, Dr. Futral, Neil Trossevin P.A., Dr. Nicholson If a patient has both Medi-Share and Multiplan/PHCS. All our providers are obligated to accept this per our contract with Multiplan. This is a rare occurrence.

Special Cases

In addition to the numerous plans our physicians accept in their office, there are also insurance cases that require you to receive and/or communicate extra information when scheduling.

  • Self-Pay o The minimum out of. pocket cost for an in-office Self Pay visit is $250. That amount is just to cover the office visit with the provider and is due at the time of service. This means that if the doctor orders labs or tests the cost may increase (labs and tests are at the doctor's discretion at the time of the visit). Document in the appointment details that you have communicated this policy to the caller It is important to share this information with callers upfront to ensure there are no surprises at the time of the visit.
  • Insurance with Referral Requirements o Depending. upon the insurance policy, a referral may or may not be necessary for an appointment. Please confirm with the caller whether it is required by their insurance. o There are three exceptions to this procedure  Kaiser- patient must bring/fax referral and provide referral number  Tricare- patient must bring/fax referral  Triwest (now Optum)- patient must bring/fax referral Patients can still schedule with us even if they do not have their referral on hand. Please encourage patient to obtain referral as you are scheduling appointment.
  • Care Credit o Care Credit is a form of payment for medical bills. not an insurance plan. Patients may or may not have an insurance policy in addition to having Care Credit. Callers using Care Credit must be informed that their out-ofpocket expense must be at least $300 before our office can accept it as a form of payment. Add to the appointment detail that the patient has Care Credit and is aware of the 300-dollar minimum.
  • Financial Assistance o Most medical facilities. offer assistance programs to ease the financial burden of medical expenses for patients in need. Some of our offices that do not accept these programs. You can clarify this information with the CBO or office’s front desk.  Wellstar Cobb Assistance- Dr. Kaplan and Dr. Oberle ▪ Add “Patient has WA” to appointment details ▪ Inform patient to bring assistance letter and add “aware to bring assistance letter” to appointment details ▪ Email patient name, date of birth, appointment, physician, and insurance information to Danielle Ledford at dledford@gaurology.com  Northside Assistance (accepted in our Northern POD, for physician’s affiliated with Northside) ▪ Add “Patient has NA” to appointment details ▪ Inform patient to bring assistance letter and “aware to bring assistance letter” to appointment details ▪ Email patient name, date of birth, appointment, physician, and insurance information to Danielle Ledford

Most advanced practioners are paired with a specific physician in our practice. For commercial insurance, determine whether an advanced practioner will accept a patient’s plan by referring to the corresponding physician’s insurance grid. Identifying Diagnoses

Urgent Diagnoses

While you are not expected to be medical experts, and prohibited from giving medical advice, it is important for you to recognize diagnoses requiring urgent appointments. To determine a condition’s urgency, consult the Telemedicine Guideline. This tool will assist your scheduling of both clinic and virtual appointment. Below is a list of diagnoses marked as urgent (24 hours-1 week) on the guideline. Review the full guideline to find additional conditions and timelines. Images sourced from Telemedicine Guideline Below are the definitions of some the urgent diagnoses indicated on the guideline

  • Epididymitis- swelling and pain in the testicles
  • Torsion- twisting of the testicles causing. blocked blood flow
  • Priapism- prolonged and/or painful erection
  • Hypogonadism- low testosterone. reduction of hormone production in the testicles
  • Hydrocele- build of fluid in one. or both testicles
  • Macrohematuria/ Gross Hematuria- visible blood in urine
  • Dysuria- painful urination
  • Pyelonephritis- UTI that generally begins in. urethra and travels to one/both kidneys Be aware that many callers will not know the name of their specific diagnosis, and because we are not clinically licensed, we cannot diagnose them. Do not make the mistake of diagnosing a patient. This can cause unnecessary fear and misinformation. Callers can, however, describe their symptoms and you add notes in the appointment details. Callers describing “pain,” “swelling,” “burning,” “infection,” or “lumps” (especially testicle/penile related) are considered as having an urgent issue.

Commonly Scheduled Diagnoses

While there is a wide range of diagnoses our providers have expertise in, becoming familiar with commonly scheduled diagnoses will help you become a more informed scheduler overall.

  • Frequency- condition that causes more than. average urination
  • Urgency- immediate unstoppable urge to urinate
  • Incontinence- loss of urine control
  • Urinary Tract Infection (UTI)- bacterial infection. in the system that processes and carries urine from the body
  • Urinary Retention- inability to empty urine. from bladder
  • Elevated PSA (prostate-specific antigen)- PSAs are. protein made by both cancerous and non-cancerous prostate cells; elevated levels can be an indicator of prostate cancer since cancerous cells tend to produce more PSAs
  • Blood in Urine- also known as. micro/trace hematuria (microscopic blood picked up on a test) or macro/gross hematuria (visible)
  • Vasectomy- minor surgery to block sperm. from reaching the semen that is ejaculated from the penis
  • Erectile Dysfunction (ED)- recurrent inability to. achieve or maintain erection
  • Prostatitis- swelling of prostate gland
  • BPH (benign prostatic hyperplasia)- also known as enlarged prostate. can cause uncomfortable urinary symptoms
  • Stones- hard deposit of mineral and. acid salts that stick together in concentrated urine
11

Stones

Gathering Key Information

As a urologic specialist group, we receive an abundant amount of kidney stone referrals on a regular basis. Kidney stones vary in size, shape and pain levels. Because there are so many variables involved with kidney stones, it is crucial that we ask patients or referring providers offices the proper questions.

  • Have you had a kidney stone before?
  • What is your current comfort level?
  • Has the patient had any recent imaging done? If so. where? Do you have a copy of the CT report/disc of the imaging you’ve had done? If not, can you bring that information/have the information faxed for your evaluation?
  • How large is the kidney stone?
  • Are you experiencing any other symptoms?. o If the patient describes any nausea or visible blood in urine, create chart first then transfer this call to triage Getting these questions answered makes treating the patient significantly easier. If you are unable to find an immediate appointment for the patient, especially if experiencing severe symptoms, reach out to Floor Support or Triage. Make sure the patient has a chart in our system before you reach out to another department!

Stones and Advanced Practioners

Depending upon the patient’s insurance, some advanced practioners are comfortable with seeing and evaluating kidney stone patients. It is crucial, however, to make sure to schedule these cases according to the provider’s preferences. Often our Physician Assistants and Nurse Practioners will have sooner openings than the physician. Reassure the caller they will be fully cared for with our advanced practioners and a doctor will be in the office as well to provide input and make final decisions. It is extremely important to check the provider’s preferences to know whether a physician’s presence is required before a stones patient is scheduled with an advanced practioner. Any time you schedule with an advanced practioner, add “patient is aware of provider” to the appointment details.

Stone Hotline

Potential stones patients also have access to our 24/7 “Kidney Stone Hotline” 1855- STONE11 (1-855-786-6311). This service allows patients to contact a representative for a same or next-day appointment. If a patient calls the Kidney Stone Hotline during regular business hours they will reach the Patient Support Center.

CONTACT

Stone11

The timeline for a Stone11 appointment is 24-48 hours from the time of the call. If a patient declines an appointment within that timeframe, and prefers something later, the appointment becomes and office visit (NP/OV/FU) not a Stone11. This is important when labeling the appointment event field. When a patient declines an appointment within the 24-48 hour timeframe, add that fact to the details for your appointment.

Stone Reduction Clinic

The “Kidney Stone Reduction Clinic” is led by Dr. Wesley Ludwig. This patient-centered clinic creates customized treatment plans that narrow down the specific individual causes of kidney stones and how patients can go about preventing them in the future. Patients interested in this service will directly request it.

  • If requested by a New Patient. schedule the consultation as a telemedicine visit with Dr. Ludwig o Add “Stone Reduction Clinic” to the appointment details
  • If requested by an Established Patient. confirmed whether they learned about this service on their own or if they were referred from their Georgia Urology provider o If referred schedule the consultation as a clinic visit with Dr. Ludwig • Add the referring physician’s name to the appointment details • Add “Stone Reduction Clinic” to the appointment details o If no referral, send patient’s information to that region’s Practice Administrator, Assistant Practice Administration, and CC your department manager

Locked Accounts and Stones Patients

This keeps the patient informed in case you must look for another appointment. This same procedure also applies to patients with a cancer diagnosis

Quality Audits

To maintain consistent patient-focused service and aid agents improve their customer service and medical scheduling skills, weekly audits are performed. Every Friday you will receive an evaluation from the Quality Auditor of three of your calls from that week. Throughout the week the Quality Auditor will review your calls, either live or recorded, send you a report detailing your completion, or lack thereof, of our procedures and protocols.

Scoring

Every call will be scored out of 100 points for call flow, and an additional 100 points for calls resulting in scheduled appointments.

  • For new hires. the graduated goal is a monthly score of at least 85% over the following five months post training. Meaning this is score you will be working toward during that time.
  • After the five post training months. the goal is a monthly score of at least 85%.

Quality Tracking

Quality will be tracked by a three-month rolling calendar approach.

  • Two months with below goal scores. in a rolling three-month period will result in the following: 1st- Verbal Warning 2nd- Written Warning 3rd- Written Warning and Performance Improvement Plan 4th- Additional Performance Management up to and including Termination Exception- If final month in a rolling three-month period goal is met, and the previous months are below goal, no additional performance management steps will be taken.
  • Making a repetitive error week over. week or month over month could result in additional performance Example A August September October November December January February 75% 79% 98% 82% 100% 65% 100% October through August – No performance issues November through September – Verbal warning for first miss December through October – No performance issues January through November – Written warning second miss February through December – No performance issues Example B August September October November December January February 76% 86% 90% 84% 100% 76% 95% October through August – No performance issues November through September – No performance issues December through October – No performance issues January through November – Verbal warning for first miss February through December – No performance issues Example C August September October November December January February 75% 85% 60% 84% 86% 78% 100% October through August – No performance issues November through September – Verbal warning for first miss December through October – Would not progress because most recent month goal was met. January through November – Written warning February through December – No performance issues -Information sourced from “Quality Guideline and PM” by Toni Harrell, Patient Support Center Manager

Electronic Health Records

Patient chart information is housed in our Electronic Health Records system. From time to time you will encounter situations that require you to take a closer look at a patient’s chart. Below are procedures for using the E.H.R. system

Opening a New Patient in E.H.R

  1. Immediately after logging in you will. be directed to select an office and physician (your actual selections do not matter, unless you are sending a phone note)
  2. Select Patient button (right of provider selection)
  3. This will open the Patient Lookup Tool. Enter demographic information and “Find” to access chart

Closing a Patient in E.H.R.

  1. File (top left)
  2. Close patient
  3. You can now pull up a. different patient by selecting the Patient button

Creating a Chart in E.H.R.

  1. Select Patient button. this will open the Patient Lookup Tool
  2. Select “New”
  3. Enter patient’s name. date of birth, address, contact number, email, PCP, and insurance information.
  4. Change patient’s Status to Active
  5. Click the Client Defined category. insert the office the patient would like to be seen in Home Location
  6. Click OK
  7. System will ask for permission to create chart. select “Ok”

Creating a Chart in Practice Management

  1. Select the “Chart” icon (directly right of Appt Book). this will open the Patient Lookup Tool
  2. Refer to 15.3. steps 2-5
  3. Click the “Chart” button
  4. System will ask. “Are you sure you would like to create a chart?” Select “Ok”
  5. A “Create Encounter” box will pop up. select “Cancel”

Using Uro_Master to Find Future Appointments

  1. Patient pull up in EHR
  2. Under the Patient History category. Select the appropriate appointment date from the encounters list (confirm date with patient)
  3. Find that encounter’s uro_master (the notes. from an office visit)
  4. Review the “Plan Order” section of. the uro_master to see if there’s a specific timeframe listed for a patient’s next visit Using Uro_Master to Determine Patient’s Physician If a patient has only seen an advanced practioner and cannot recall which physician they need to follow up with. Uro_master can help verify which physician a patient should be seeing. Refer to the bottom of the uro_master for the associated physician’s signature.

Radiology Orders – images ordered by our providers

  1. Patient pull up in EHR
  2. Select encounter date (confirm with patient)
  3. Select GUA Rad Sched
  4. Check for Facility name and location
  5. Check for a GAU Contact name
  6. If patient is inquiring about scheduling their radiology. provide them with the Facility’s number (you may have to google this) o If no Facility listed, reach out to GAU Contact o If issues at Facility reach out to GAU Contact
  7. If no GAU Contact listed. reach out to triage
  8. If no order. reach out to triage

HIPPA/Authorization Forms

  1. Patient pull up in EHR
  2. In the Patient History category. search through the encounters for the Phreesia “Release of Information” form
  3. Check for additional names/relations indicated on. form o If caller’s name differs from person listed on form, apologize to caller and inform that their requested information cannot be provided  Do not share names of listed authorized individuals
  4. If patients want to change their authorization form. they must come in and do so physically

Medical Records

Before you begin your search, ask the medical records follow up questions listed in Chapter 6, 6.6 Medical Records Service

  1. Patient pull up in EHR
  2. Select “Categories”
  3. Open “External Chart” (click all documents. under this tab if necessary) o Depending on type of record it could have its own category (ex: pathology, labs, referrals)
  4. If records not present reach out to front desk and inquire. they will let you know if patient needs to refax them o If patient needs to refax records, verify the fax number and receiving location with patient

Pharmacy Changes in Practice Management (PM)

  1. Open patient in People Lookup Tool. in NextGen PM
  2. Select the “Pharmacy” category
  3. Select a yellow folder
  4. Select “New,” this will open the. Pharmacy Lookup tool
  5. Enter Pharmacy name (confirm details with. patient) and select “Find”
  6. Select the appropriate pharmacy. confirm address with the patient o If patient’s pharmacy does not pull up in NextGen database contact triage
  7. Select “OK”

Pharmacy Changes in E.H.R.

  1. 10 Pharmacy Changes in E.H.R.
  2. Patient pull up in E.H.R
  3. Select “Patient Demographics”
  4. Under the “PCP/Primary Practice Provider/Pharmacy” category. select the box directly under “Pharmacy #1” or “Pharmacy #2”
  5. Refer to 15.9. steps 2-7

Patient Portal Enrollment

We are no longer using enrollment tokens, if a patient has received a token number in the past and needs another link you must use the email enrollment

  1. Patient pull up in EHR
  2. Select Patient Portal icon. this will open Patient Portal Enrollment tool
  3. Verify enrollment status (Completed. Not Enrolled, Pending, Locked) o Completed- patient is successfully enrolled in Patient Portal o Not enrolled- patients needs email enrollment link A. Confirm patient’s email and update if needed B. Make sure “Email enrollment link” is selected and select “Ok” o Pending- patient can be sent another link to complete enrollment A. Click “Revoke” B. Confirm patient’s email and update if needed C. Make sure “Email enrollment link” is selected and select “OK” o If Pending and patient initially sent a token- email enrollment link must be used instead. A. Click “Revoke” B. Confirm patient’s email and update if needed C. Make sure “Email enrollment link” is selected and select “OK” D. Select “Yes” to message asking if you want to cancel the token enrollment process and proceed with email enrollment o Locked- occurs after four failed login attempts by patient A. Select “File” B. Select “Patient Portal” C. Select “Enrollment” D. Select “Unlock Patient”

Finding Missed Callers and Chart Footprints

  1. In Practice Management. Select the “Chart” icon, this will open the Patient Lookup Tool
  2. Input patient demographics and search for patient. Patient’s chart will pop open
  3. Select the “Clinical History/ Notes” tab
  4. Under the “Topics” category on the leftmost side. expand “History”
  5. Select “Chart”
  6. Users that have accessed that chart. will generate in a list with the most recent date at the top o If the patient knows the exact time they were contacted, look for a match next to a “Creator” name o If the patient does not know the exact time they were contacted, begin at the top of the list, and work your way down If a provider is listed, do not reach out directly. Skip this entry and continue working down If patient is adamant that they were contacted by the physician, then reach out to provider’s nurse

Care Transferring Telephone Notes

Each provider has their own preference on whether a phone note is required for transfer patients. Check the physician preference tool prior to scheduling.

  1. Patient pull up in EHR
  2. Change location to Call Center
  3. Change provider to MD patient wants. to transfer to
  4. Go to the “Patient History” category. If there is no encounter for the current day, select “New”
  5. Highlight the encounter for the current day
  6. Select the telephone icon
  7. Select “Other,” this will open a. editable template for you to create a message
  8. In “Contact Type,” choose the type. of communication you had with the patient, most of the time it will be “Incoming Call”
  9. Identify who you spoke with o If you spoke with the patient. check the box next to “Patient” o If you did not speak with the patient, type the name of the caller and click in the “Relationship” box to choose how the caller is connected to the patient
  10. Add message to Comments section o. “Above listed patient would like to transfer their care due to location/personal reasons. Is this ok?
  11. Select “Send & Close,” this will. open the “Select Task Recipient” tool
  12. Search for the recipient provider and. select “Add.” The will move the selected person to the “Task Recipient” box.
  13. Select “Ok.” Your note will then. be sent to the selected provider.
  14. To create a ticket for your message. select “Preview Document . o Your ticket will automatically pop open, and an icon for it will appear in current encounter
  15. Wait for reply o Provider approves-. Use steps 1-14 to send a new telephone note to physician patient is transferring from  “Above listed patient has transferred their care” o Provider denies- Contact patient and inform “Provider is not taking on new patients at this time.” If the patient is seeking a care transfer and needs an emergency appt, it is often best that the issue is resolved with current provider first.

Online Communication Systems

Patient Portal

The Patient Portal a communication tool between patients and their providers. Patients have the option to view test results, submit medication refill requests, and ask nonurgent questions to their physician. Patient Portal Enrollment Sometimes you will receive calls from patients needing assistance enrolling/reenrolling into the portal. We can email enrollment links through our Electronic Health Records system. Refer to Chapter 15, 15.11 Patient Portal Enrollment. For patients with significant patient portal issues, send an email to the PSC’s Portal Assistance team (portalassistance@gaurology.com).

CONTACT

For patients with significant patient portal issues, send an email to the PSC’s Portal Assistance team (portalassistance@gaurology.com).

Phreesia

We utilize a pre-visit check-in system called Phreesia. This system allows the office staff to check-in and check-out patients, keep track of how long a patient has been checked into the office, document the collection of copays and balances, provide new patient forms, and pre-screen patients for COVID-19. It also automatically sends pre-visit check in notifications and forms to patients via email or text message. • As you are scheduling you will need to make patients aware to expect their patient forms two days prior to their appointment. All paperwork and copayments can be completed online. Additionally, include “patient is aware to complete paperwork prior” to the appointment details. In the event you schedule a same day or next day appointment, the Floor Support team is authorized to expedite this process by “pushing” those forms up to a week out from the scheduled appointment date. After making the appointment, simply send an email to phreesiasamenextday@gaurology.com with the patient's name, date of birth, email, and cell. Some patients prefer not to use our online system. In those cases, advise them to come fifteen minutes early to their appointment to complete their paperwork with the front desk. Include “patient declined online paperwork” to the appointment details.

CONTACT

After making the appointment, simply send an email to phreesiasamenextday@gaurology.com with the patient's name, date of birth, email, and cell.

Phone Systems

You will be equipped with a personal phone, headset, direct extension. The Patient Support Center phones go live at 8:30 am. You are expected to login no later than 8:35am. Below are the procedures for using the phone system.

Logging In

  1. Select Hot Desk
  2. Select Login
  3. Enter your extension
  4. Press Ok
  5. System will ask for PIN. this is the same number as your extension
  6. Press Ok
  7. Your Name should appear on the phone
  8. Headset button should be lit if. headset is being used

Outgoing Calls

  1. Press button next to your extension number
  2. Dial a. Dial an extension to reach GU employee or department b. Dial 9 + 10 digit number for in-state calls c. Dial 9+ 1+ 10 digit number for out-of-state call

Transferring Calls

  1. Press black button to direct right. of red button
  2. Dial extension/number a. Merge call- Reselect black button to direct right of red button b. Retrieve call- Black button with circled X c. Transfer call- select Release Me button

Retrieving Numbers from Past Calls

  1. Press Blue button
  2. Select Call History
  3. Select Chose Made/Answered
  4. Select Person
  5. Close to exit

Extension Directory

  1. Select Phone book
  2. Enter 1st 3 letters of last name
  3. Look up desired name and extension
  4. Call

Placing Caller on Hold

  1. Press Red button a. Select button (bottom left) that displays phone number to take caller off hold
  2. While on a call. you can place a held caller back on hold by picking up and line and quickly reselecting the hold button.

Mute

  1. Select clear microphone button

Disconnecting Calls

  1. Press Black button with circled X a. You should see your unlit extension in the bottom left corner if successfully disconnected

Logging Out

  1. 3rd button from top left

Make Busy Codes- places you in a Do Not Disturb mode

  1. 2nd button from bottom left
  2. Enter corresponding 1-9 (excluding 7) Make. Busy codes listed below
  3. Restroom
  4. Lunch
  5. Computer/Phone Issues
  6. After Call
  7. Patient Reschedules or Projects
  8. Meeting
  9. Break
  10. No Show Appointments
